item.title: Oil prices inch back up as Iran and the Houthis escalate threats
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Global oil prices, which had dropped about 20% in recent weeks with the U.S.-Iran war locked in a stalemate, have risen again slightly as Tehran threatens to increase attacks on ships and fighting between its Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia escalates.Ship transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen again this month and the amount of oil and other products being shipped out of the Persian Gulf remains at just over half of pre-war levels, according to shipping intelligence firm Kpler.The Iran-backed Houthi group claimed an attack on the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital on Wednesday, as well on a sprawling oil refinery in the country's east.
New Updates
53m ago
Body of Jordanian sailor found off UAE coast after vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz
The body of a Jordanian sailor who was reported missing after an Iranian attack on his vessel in the Strait of Hormuz last week, was found off the coast of Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates, Jordan's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.
"The body of Mohamed Hossam al-Din al-Otaibi, may he rest in peace, was found on Wednesday," the ministry said.
The United Arab Emirates' state-owned ADNOC energy company reported the sailor missing last week after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. It said 11 crew members were injured in the attack.
The Jordanian ministry praised the efforts of UAE and Omani authorities for locating the sailor's body.

item.title: Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser
item.description:
Ukraine has used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone for the first time, a senior military adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Wednesday, marking a potentially significant development in the country's effort to defend cities from Russia's daily aerial attacks.
The interception was carried out using the Blysk laser air defense system, which was developed and manufactured by Ukrainian defense technology firm Carmine Sky. Technology for laser air defense systems is being developed as part of the wider Private Air Defense program, Zelenskyy's adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said in a statement.
About 100 companies across Ukraine have joined the government-backed private air defense initiative.
Russia started deploying jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine earlier this year. The weapons travel faster, making them harder to intercept than the more common propeller-driven attack drones.
In June, Ukraine was only intercepting about 57% of the jet-powered drones, reflecting a significant vulnerability as Ukrainian forces had been shooting down about 90% of the conventional Russian attack drones.
Russia has increasingly used its Geran-4 and Geran-5 jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine. Come Back Alive, a Ukrainian military nonprofit group, told CBS News in September that Russia was likely to produce some 1,200 Geran-4 and 800 Geran-5 drones during that month alone, and it projected those numbers would grow each month.
A downed Russian Geran-4 turbojet-powered one-way attack drone is displayed at the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Oct. 29, 2026.

item.title: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway
item.description:
Cairo — A massive fire on an Egyptian highway killed 31 people and injured 21 others after a car slammed into a fuel tanker truck at high speed, Egypt's Public Prosecution office said Thursday.
The driver has been arrested, according to the statement. At least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, were destroyed in the fire.
The prosecutor said the suspect admitted causing the accident while driving around 70 miles per hour on a major highway in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, which is part of the Greater Cairo area.
A fire burns at the site where a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Al-Warraq district of Giza, Egypt, Nov. 25, 2026, in a screengrab obtained from social media video.
Habiba Abd El Aziz/REUTERS
The driver said he was changing lanes and overtaking vehicles when the front-left side of his car struck the rear-right side of the tanker, according to the prosecutor's statement, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course."
When the car hit the truck, one of the truck's tires exploded, causing it to overturn and slam into a concrete barrier.
Gasoline then leaked from the tanker and caught on fire. Images of the blaze on social media showed multiple vehicles on fire as flames and smoke billowed into the night sky.
The prosecutor said the suspect was being questioned to establish the circumstances of the accident and assess any criminal responsibility.
"It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire," Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic behind the accident, told The Associated Press. "It was a shocking scene."
Sameer told the AP he saw at least eight bodies being removed from charred vehicles....

item.title: Andy Taylor, longtime Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
item.description:
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran — whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" — and who were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor died following a "courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family and the band said in a joint statement posted to social media. He died Monday at his home surrounded by friends and family.
"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his family said.
Andy Taylor of Duran Duran with guitars in Maison Rouge Studios in London in July 1984.
Virginia Turbett/Redferns via Getty Images
On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
His family said Wednesday that Taylor "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination until the very end, never losing his love of life."
The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

item.title: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war
item.description:
More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died since Vladimir Putin ordered Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, according to leaked Russian government data analyzed by CBS News partner network BBC News. Another organization's analysis of the vast dataset suggests the toll is likely closer to 700,000.
A recent hack by pro-Ukraine groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow produced the data that was analyzed by the BBC and independent Russian outlet Mediazona. It included more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, according to the British broadcaster.
The data, which includes granular information on the location of deaths in Ukraine and Russian border regions, age ranges, causes of death, and employment and court rulings suggests at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died during the war so far, according to the BBC. According to Mediazona's analysis, which the outlet said accounted for delays in death registrations, missing records and deaths occurring since the data was leaked, Russia's total military death toll has likely reached around 700,000.
In May, the head of the United Kingdom's communications and cyber spy agency also put the number of Russian military deaths during the war at about 500,000, citing Western intelligence.
"Putin is going backwards on the battlefield, with new intelligence showing that almost half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the conflict began," Anne Keast-Butler, the director of the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ), said at the time.
Soldiers carry the coffin of 20-year-old Russian serviceman Nikita Avrov during his funeral at a church in Luga, south of St. Petersburg, April 11, 2022, after his death during the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: "Narco sub" seized in Atlantic but no drugs found on board
item.description:
The French navy intercepted a semi-submersible craft suspected of involvement in drug trafficking in the Atlantic Ocean, a prosecutor said Wednesday, days after stopping a similar "narco sub" carrying several tons of cocaine.
"The semi-submersible was flying no flag and was suspected of being involved in drug trafficking" when French forces intercepted it on November 17, said organized crime prosecutor Vanessa Perree.
No drugs were found but "the vessel's location, lack of flag, its clandestine nature and items discovered onboard" led to the arrest of two crew members, she added.
The operation was carried out in cooperation with the Colombian navy and the U.S. Joint Interagency Task Force South.
The vessel's seizure "deals a serious blow to the drug traffickers' logistics." said Perree.
Catherine Vautrin, the country's armed forces minister, hailed the operation in a social media post, which included images of the vessel.
The French navy intercepted a semi-submersible craft suspected of involvement in drug trafficking in the Atlantic Ocean, officials said.
Catherine Vautrin, France's armed forces minister
"The French armed forces are maintaining their efforts in the fight against drug trafficking networks," she wrote on X. "With this intervention by the Armed Forces in the French Antilles, an entire criminal network and its associated logistics have been disrupted."
Narco subs, which cannot go fully underwater, are popular among international drug traffickers as they can sometimes elude detection by law enforcement.

item.title: Titanic postcard sent days before doomed voyage sells for pricey sum
item.description:
A rare postcard from a Titanic crew member that features the famed ocean liner and was sent less than a week before its doomed voyage in 1912 sold at auction for over $41,000, according to a U.K. auction house.
The postcard from Jack Phillips, the Titanic's chief radio officer, was postmarked April 6, 1912, four days before the ill-fated ship set sail on its maiden voyage across the Atlantic from Southampton, England, for New York City.
Phillips, who turned 25 on the ship, sent the postcard to his sister, Elsie Phillips, according to auction house Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
"Thanks very much for your letter. Having glorious weather, went to Cowes yesterday. Will write later before we sail. Love all, Jack," Phillips wrote on the back of the postcard.
Jack Phillips wrote to his sister, Elsie Phillips, on a Titanic postcard that was postmarked April 6, 1912.
Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
The front features a picture of the Titanic at Southampton in southern England. The auction house said the postcard was in "very good to fine condition, with some light soiling and toning."
The Titanic is seen on a postcard that was postmarked April 6, 1912.
Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
According to the auction house, the postcard sold for 32,000 British pounds, or around $41,800. With taxes and fees, the final cost was 40,000 pounds, or around $52,300.
During the trans-Atlantic crossing, on the night of April 14, 1912, the Titanic struck an iceberg and eventually sank, killing over 1,500 people.
